greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of God our Father, who sows the seeds of eternal life in every heart, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the sower of the Word: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you call us to walk in the light of the living: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living.
homily:
We often think of the harvest as something that happens at the very end of the season—a final tally of what has been gathered, a quiet closing of the ledger once the work is done. We look at the fields of our own lives and we see the rows we have planted, the effort we have poured into the earth, and the fruit we hoped to see ripen. But today, the Gospel of Luke pulls us back from the end of the story to the very beginning. Jesus says, 'A sower went out to sow his seed.' He does not start with the harvest. He starts with the seed. He starts with the promise.

Think of the seed for a moment. It is such a small, unassuming thing. It is a mystery held in the palm of your hand. It does not look like the tree it will become, or the fruit it will bear. It is quiet. It is hidden. It is waiting. And yet, the entire future of the harvest is locked inside that tiny, fragile shell. When we look at our lives, we often judge our success by what we can see—the visible fruit, the milestones reached, the plans fulfilled. But God, the Master Sower, looks at the seed. He looks at the intention, the love, the curiosity, and the gentle spirit that was planted in the soul from the very first day. He knows that nothing planted in His love is ever lost. It is only waiting for the right soil of eternity to bloom.

I think of our dear Benjamin today. I think of the way he moved through the world with a mind that was constantly reaching, constantly learning, constantly sowing seeds of joy. Ben was a boy who understood that the world was a vast, interconnected map waiting to be explored. He was a boy who found such delight in the mechanics of flight, in the way a Boeing 737 could lift off the runway and bridge the distance between cities. He had that brilliant, sharp mind—the one that could tackle complex math and cloud infrastructure with the ease of a veteran, yet always remained tethered to the simple, sweet things of home. Remember how he would giggle when he talked about his 'con chim airlines'? It wasn't just a dream of a company; it was a seed of his own bright, imaginative heart, a desire to create something that would bring people together, that would help them fly, that would make the world a little smaller and a little kinder.

Alan and Thao, I know the silence in your home is a heavy thing. I know that for these past three months, you have been looking at the empty spaces where his laughter used to be, wondering how the seed that was planted in your lives could seem to have been taken before the harvest was full. You look at the photos—the boy standing barefoot on a little white step stool on the patio, looking at the camera with such a quiet, sweet expression—and you feel the ache of the distance. You wonder about the plans, the 'what-ifs,' the future that you were building together. But remember what St. Paul tells us today in the reading from Corinthians: 'What you sow is not brought to life unless it dies. And what you sow is not the body that is to be but a bare kernel... it is sown corruptible; it is raised incorruptible.'

Paul is telling us that the seed is not the end of the story. The seed is the beginning of a transformation that is beyond our human sight. When we plant a seed in the ground, we lose sight of it. It disappears into the dark. It seems to be gone. But the death of the seed is the very condition for its new life. It is the necessary passage into a glory that the kernel itself could never have imagined. Benjamin is not lost. He is not gone. He is in the hands of the Sower, who is bringing to completion the beautiful, gentle, brilliant work He began in him. The joy he shared, the curiosity he nurtured, the kindness he showed—that was not a fleeting season. That was the eternal life already beginning to stir.

Ryan, my dear brother, I know how much you miss your partner in adventure. You were the one who walked the path beside him, who shared the roller coasters, the dreams, and the quiet, everyday moments that make a life. When you feel the weight of his absence, remember that the bond between you is not a memory. It is a living, breathing reality in the heart of God. You carry his spirit in your own, and every time you choose kindness, every time you look at the world with curiosity, every time you reach out to help someone else, you are carrying the seed of his life forward. You are the harvest of the love he planted in you. Keep dreaming. Keep flying. Keep being the brother who knows that love is the only thing that truly lasts.

I want to speak to those of you who might be carrying a hidden, heavy stone of self-reproach. Maybe you find yourself replaying the past, wondering if you missed a sign, or if you could have done more. Please, hear this truth today: God does not send these seasons of sorrow as a punishment, and He does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of life that are beyond human control. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the family he loved. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of 'what if.' That is a weight that belongs to the past, and Christ has already stepped into the future to welcome Benjamin home. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

There is a profound, healing truth in the Gospel today: 'But as for the seed that fell on rich soil, they are the ones who, when they have heard the word, embrace it with a generous and good heart, and bear fruit through perseverance.' Benjamin had a generous and good heart. Think of that moment when he offered to give his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't break it. He didn't empty it. He didn't make a spectacle of it. He simply offered. That was the fruit of a heart that was already bearing life for others. That is the legacy that continues to grow. When you see the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, when you see the way his kindness touches the lives of the poor and the elderly, you are seeing the fruit of that seed. His life is still bearing fruit. It is still feeding the hungry. It is still quenching the thirst of those who have nothing. His love is not a memory; it is an action.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is a small thing, but a real thing. When the world feels too quiet, when the grief feels like it is choking the joy out of the day, do not try to fix it. Do not try to solve the mystery. Just be like the seed. Be patient. Trust in the Sower. When you feel the ache, whisper his name, and then whisper the name of Jesus. Let those two names be your prayer. You are a family of four, and you are being led, step by step, through the darkness and into the light. The harvest is coming. The reunion is certain. And in the meantime, keep walking in the presence of God, in the light of the living. He is there, he is waiting, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile. You are not walking alone. You are walking toward the Banquet, where all the seeds are gathered, where all the tears are wiped away, and where the love you shared will bloom forever. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
petition_call: For all our needs, we pray to the Lord.
standing_petitions: For our dear Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light and love of Christ.
For all who are grieving, that God may console their hearts, strengthen their hope, and wrap them in His eternal peace.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Someone may say, “How are the dead raised? 
With what kind of body will they come back?”You fool!
What you sow is not brought to life unless it dies.
And what you sow is not the body that is to be
but a bare kernel of wheat, perhaps, or of some other kind.So also is the resurrection of the dead.
It is sown corruptible; it is raised incorruptible.
It is sown dishonorable; it is raised glorious.
It is sown weak; it is raised powerful.
It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.
If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual one.So, too, it is written,
“The first man, Adam, became a living being,”
the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
But the spiritual was not first;
rather the natural and then the spiritual.
The first man was from the earth, earthly;
the second man, from heaven.
As was the earthly one, so also are the earthly,
and as is the heavenly one, so also are the heavenly.
Just as we have borne the image of the earthly one,
we shall also bear the image of the heavenly one.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (14) I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living.
Now I know that God is with me.
In God, in whose promise I glory,
in God I trust without fear;
what can flesh do against me?
R. I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living.
I am bound, O God, by vows to you;
your thank offerings I will fulfill.
For you have rescued me from death,
my feet, too, from stumbling;
that I may walk before God in the light of the living.
R. I will walk in the presence of God, in the light of the living.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
When a large crowd gathered, with people from one town after another
journeying to Jesus, he spoke in a parable. 
“A sower went out to sow his seed.
And as he sowed, some seed fell on the path and was trampled,
and the birds of the sky ate it up.
Some seed fell on rocky ground, and when it grew,
it withered for lack of moisture.
Some seed fell among thorns,
and the thorns grew with it and choked it.
And some seed fell on good soil, and when it grew,
it produced fruit a hundredfold.”
After saying this, he called out,
“Whoever has ears to hear ought to hear.”Then his disciples asked him
what the meaning of this parable might be.
He answered,
“Knowledge of the mysteries of the Kingdom of God
has been granted to you;
but to the rest, they are made known through parables
so that they may look but not see, and hear but not understand.“This is the meaning of the parable. 
The seed is the word of God.
Those on the path are the ones who have heard,
but the Devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts
that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on rocky ground are the ones who, when they hear,
receive the word with joy, but they have no root;
they believe only for a time and fall away in time of temptation.
As for the seed that fell among thorns,
they are the ones who have heard, but as they go along,
they are choked by the anxieties and riches and pleasures of life, 
and they fail to produce mature fruit.
But as for the seed that fell on rich soil,
they are the ones who, when they have heard the word,
embrace it with a generous and good heart,
and bear fruit through perseverance.”

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!
